name: Backpacking Checklist
description: A multi-day backpacking checklist covering the pack, shelter and sleep system, food, water treatment and lightweight gear.

items.text: Backpacking pack sized for your trip length
Pack rain cover or a pack liner
Stuff sacks and dry bags to organize gear
Hip-belt pockets for snacks and small items
Trekking poles
items.note: Poles ease the load on long climbs and descents.

items.text: Lightweight tent, tarp, or hammock
Footprint or ground sheet
Sleeping bag or quilt rated for the conditions
Insulated sleeping pad
Compact inflatable pillow
Stakes, guy lines, and a small repair kit
Lightweight stove and fuel canister
Lighter and backup matches
Pot and a long spork
Dehydrated or no-cook meals planned per day
Calorie-dense snacks: bars, nuts, dried fruit
Bear canister or hang bag where required
items.note: Store all food and scented items away from your sleep area.

items.text: Water filter or purifier
Chemical tablets as a backup method
Collapsible bottles or a hydration reservoir
Dirty-water bag for collecting from sources
Notes on water sources along your route
Moisture-wicking base layers
Insulating jacket (down or synthetic)
Waterproof, breathable rain shell
Quick-dry hiking pants or convertible pants
Extra socks and underwear
Warm hat, gloves, and a buff
Camp shoes or lightweight sandals
Map, compass, and route notes
GPS or phone with offline maps and a power bank
Headlamp with extra batteries
First-aid kit with blister care
Emergency shelter and a whistle
Permits and any required documentation
Check the forecast and conditions and share your route
items.note: Tell someone your itinerary and expected return.

items.text: Trowel, toilet paper, and a waste bag
Travel toothbrush and biodegradable soap
Hand sanitizer and wet wipes
Sunscreen, lip balm, and insect repellent
Repair tape, cordage, and a small multi-tool
Sewing kit or gear-specific patch kit

faq.q: What do I need for a multi-day backpacking trip?
faq.a: You need a backpacking pack, a lightweight tent or tarp, a sleeping bag and pad, a compact stove, food, and a water-treatment method. Add layered clothing, navigation, a first-aid kit, and a way to call for help, choosing the lightest version of each item.

faq.q: How is backpacking different from hiking?
faq.a: Hiking usually means a day on the trail with a small daypack, while backpacking means carrying multi-day gear, including shelter, sleep, and food, and camping overnight in the backcountry. Backpacking demands more planning around weight, water, and food.

faq.q: How do I treat water while backpacking?
faq.a: Use a pump or squeeze filter, a UV purifier, or chemical tablets to make backcountry water safe to drink. Carry a primary method plus a lightweight backup, and plan your route around reliable water sources.

faq.q: Can I print this backpacking checklist?
faq.a: Yes. You can print the checklist or download it as a PDF, then tick off each item as you load your pack and check your total weight.

faq.q: How heavy should my backpack be?
faq.a: Many backpackers aim to keep a loaded pack around 20 percent of body weight or less, not counting food and water. Choose lightweight, multi-use gear, repackage food, and leave behind anything you will not realistically use.
